Subject: Price-approval backlog + stale deals — action & forecast impact

Team,

Quick heads-up as we lock Q3 numbers this week: we have three mid-to-large deals (Velocis — VEL-2027-003, BluePeak, and NorthBridge) sitting in "Legal/Price Approval" or "Procurement Review" for >7 business days. These pending discount approvals are already affecting our committed forecast. Finance has flagged Velocis specifically because procurement asked for a 25% concession versus the approved price band.

Action items:
- Ben: please confirm the exact discount requested and attach the AM notes (I need visibility by EOD Thu).
- Karthik: can you run the incremental margin calc and confirm if we can accommodate a one-time concession without moving it to "up-for-review" in forecast guidance? (see attached pricing_workbook_Q3.xlsx)
- Vanessa: if there's a request to escalate to Deal Desk or to legal for new terms, escalate by Friday noon so we can capture in the Commit roll-up.

Important: if an approval is still pending at the time of the weekly commit snapshot, Finance will mark the deal as "conditional" (50% weight) in the formal forecast. We want to avoid surprise hits to the booked/committed numbers.

Attach: pricing_workbook_Q3.xlsx (worksheet with simple margin sensitivity)

Thanks — please keep replies inline and short so I can run a consolidated note to Finance.

— Monica

Subject: Re: Price-approval backlog + stale deals — action & forecast impact

Ben/Monica —

Reviewed the workbook and ran a quick sensitivity on Velocis: if we accept 25% off list and assume standard run-rate, incremental margin compresses from 42% to ~25% (see velocis_calc.pdf I'm attaching). Two notes:
1) If we treat this as a volume-based rebate (payback tied to usage) we can protect NRR and spread the hit over 12 months; finance can still count a higher portion of the deal as committed.
2) If the concession requires a contractual term change (custom SLA or data-retention language), legal will add 7–10 business days which pushes signature past our snapshot.

Recommendation: approve as a structured rebate (term sheet addendum) and set a conditional commit at 75% in the forecast until the rebate triggers. That keeps the commit closer to reality and avoids a full 50% drop.

Attachment: velocis_calc.pdf

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Finance (Revenue) — Redwood Inference

Looping everyone to close the loop and make the call for the weekly commit:

Summary / decision path:
- Ben: PR#789 accepted into Deal Desk queue; AM notes received. Velocis procurement (Nora) confirms they want the concession tied to a 12-month usage commit (see her inline note below).
- Karthik: Finance recommends a structured rebate approach and to mark the deal at 75% commit until rebate triggers. Agreed.
- Vanessa: please note — escalate to legal only if Velocis requests custom contract language. Otherwise Deal Desk should handle the rebate amendment.

Forecast treatment: Finance will treat VEL-2027-003 as 75% committed for the official snapshot on Monday. If a signed amendment is received before the snapshot, we will move to 100% committed.

Next steps (owners + deadlines):
- Ben: confirm procurement's signed amendment or an explicit signature date by Monday 09:00 PT.
- Karthik: run final impact to margin and confirm the accounting treatment (rebate vs. list discount) by Monday 12:00 PT.
- Vanessa: watch for legal gate and escalate if language changes are requested.

Thanks all — please reply only if your deliverable will miss the deadline. I will update Finance and include the 75% commit flag.

— Monica

Redwood Inference
